project.name: Price Calculator
project.summary: A generic, organization-branded estimator with configurable item catalogs and branching forms, administrator-reviewed supplier Excel data, multilingual indicative ranges and immutable results. Prove renovation in a hosted app first, then website embedding within launch scope.

evidence.summary: Initial product idea: branching selections, item codes, supplier-backed price range, classifications and branding.
Estimator-only correction: intermediary assists consumer, imports supplier sheets, no supplier discovery or selection.
Internal code mapping, item hierarchy, organization administration and generic industry scope.
Renovation is the first proving journey while the product remains generic.
Accepted supplier endpoint arithmetic, organization privacy, configurable quantity rules, public/assisted access and admin imports first.
Hosted app first and embedding next at launch, with flexible separate admin/calculator hosting.
Four named launch languages and acceptance of remaining item, band, publication, snapshot/PDF and multiple-calculator recommendations.
Proceeding acceptance while draft was still being prepared; no unseen synthesis confirmation.
Installed UI profile defaults: responsive accessible browser UI, no analytics, editable organization branding.
Installed secure-browser default: admin BFF session, provider selection assigned, public calculator needs no admin session.
Installed modularity and vertical-slice defaults: consumer-owned boundaries, bridges and outcome-based delivery.
Proposed Forms/Localization adapters retain consumer domain meaning; exact package/provider selections belong to architecture.

evidence.locator: Strategic analysis — proposed, not accepted architecture
evidence.summary: Three proposed contexts, revision-pinning consistency and separation of business models from delivery channels.
Named architecture, feature and deployment owners/triggers close remaining technical details without inventing production policy.

facts.statement: Suppliers are private organization entities; their product codes map to organization-owned internal item codes through administrator-managed mappings.
Sum per-item quantity times lowest/highest eligible comparable supplier unit prices into total endpoints; optional average sums quantity times per-item mean. Totals may mix suppliers.
Admins label percentage boundaries within the total min/max range; quality remains item categorization, separate from price bands.
Launch languages are Dutch, English, French and German.
Budget feasibility is the consumer outcome; real supplier selection is later business activity outside this app's v1 scope.

included.statement: Multiple named, branded calculators per organization with private authenticated central administration and separately hostable public delivery.
Core item fields, three-level category hierarchy with optional third level, category-specific typed attributes, configurable units and mapped supplier offers.
Administrator Excel import, mapping, validation preview and acceptance of comparable unit/currency/tax-normalized supplier data; one currency per calculator.
Conditional branches and configurable quantity rules, item overview, price ranges, optional means and total-range classifications.
Draft/validate/preview/publish, coherent calculation versions and visible incomplete results for missing eligible prices.
Save submission snapshots for organization admins; provide consumer PDF without account/email requirement and without supplier identities.
Assisted and independent no-account estimation through hosted and embedded calculators; hosted full app first, embedded website next, both at launch.
Four-language admin and calculator UI, form/item/classification content, historical estimate views and PDFs.
Industry-independent product configuration from launch; initial end-to-end proving journey uses renovation.

excluded.statement: Consumer supplier discovery, contact, matching and selection are excluded.
Binding quotation acceptance, payments, ordering and procurement are outside the estimator boundary.
Public supplier records and cross-organization sharing of commercial data are excluded.

deferred.statement: Supplier self-upload follows proven administrator import/template workflows in a later release; intermediary review is required before uploaded prices influence estimates.
Custom domains are deferred; hosted calculator links and existing-website embedding remain launch requirements.

actors.statement: Organization administrator manages private items, suppliers, mappings, calculators, languages, publication and saved estimates.
Intermediary guides the consumer through an assessment and may also be an organization administrator.
Consumer views an assisted estimate or independently fills a public calculator and downloads a result without account/email prerequisites.
Supplier delivers an Excel sheet offline to the administrator in v1; there is no supplier self-service or consumer interaction.
Website publisher installs the organization's calculator in an existing website after the hosted app proves its first journey.

quality_requirements.statement: Enforce organization/resource authorization across admin reads/writes, imports, published release resolution and historical access; supplier data never reaches consumer views/PDFs.
Preserve answers, items, quantities, resolved language, monetary results and calculation/revision references; later edits cannot rewrite earlier estimates.
Compare compatible units/currency/tax bases, reject unresolved supplier mapping and visibly indicate missing-price incompleteness.
Keep industry semantics configurable; acceptance must distinguish renovation example content from fixed code assumptions.
Apply responsive phone/tablet/desktop and keyboard/touch accessibility, WCAG 2.2 AA target, reduced motion and no implicit analytics.
Hosted and embedded results use shared domain calculations and publication references; admin authentication must not be required for public estimation.

integrations.statement: Suppliers deliver Excel files to administrator import; exact schema, parser, limits and replacement policy are assigned to architecture/import specification.
Existing customer websites embed a published calculator; site technology, allowed origins and exact mechanism are assigned before the embed implementation.
Consumer download renders saved estimate information into PDF; renderer/access mechanism is assigned to the result specification.

choices.decision: Generic industry estimator with renovation as the initial proving journey.
choices.rationale: User knows renovation and explicitly requires generic configuration at launch.

choices.decision: Use eligible per-item minimum/maximum unit prices times quantity and additive total endpoints; optional average is the sum of quantity times item mean.
choices.rationale: Accepted indicative-budget semantics; no promise of a single supplier fulfilling the total.

choices.decision: Admins configure labels and percentage boundaries for the total range initially.
choices.rationale: Accepted distinction between price classifications and quality categorization.

choices.decision: Private organization data with authenticated central admins and multiple published calculators.
choices.rationale: Each organization controls its own supplier commercial data and calculator configuration.

choices.decision: Administrator imports in v1; supplier self-upload later with intermediary review.
choices.rationale: Prove mapping/template quality before external upload access.

choices.decision: Hosted full web app first, embedding next within launch scope; allow separate admin/calculator hosting.
choices.rationale: First and next customers need different delivery modes without duplicate pricing behavior.

choices.decision: Save historical estimate snapshots and offer consumer PDF without account/email or supplier details.
choices.rationale: Accepted need for admin review and usable historical consumer results.

choices.decision: Support Dutch, English, French and German throughout launch experiences and content.
choices.rationale: Explicit language list, not inferred from development language or regional defaults.

choices.decision: Use draft/validate/preview/publish and review imports; visibly mark unpriced items/incomplete estimates.
choices.rationale: Protect live calculators and avoid false complete totals.

choices.decision: Adopt ui-experience-v1, no analytics, accessible responsive UI, native CSS tokens and default Lucide icons.
choices.rationale: Installed browser profile applies; organization branding remains configurable and defaults can be revised at review.

choices.decision: Use a focused journey for public estimation and product-shell layout for central administration.
choices.rationale: Different tasks need different presentation while sharing product semantics.

choices.decision: Apply bff-cookie-v1 and inherited threat/security evidence profiles to authenticated admin.
choices.rationale: Secure-browser profile applies; public estimates/embeds do not use admin sessions.

choices.decision: Use outcome-based slices with domain-owned contracts and bridges.
choices.rationale: Installed vertical-slicing/modularity guidance fits the evidenced lifecycle boundaries.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Own item code/name/unit, three category levels, typed attributes and language meaning; no generic form schema becomes the catalog model.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Project-owned catalog model; persistence provider selected in architecture.

capability_assessments.need: Supplier Excel import and code mapping
capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Own supplier identity, product-code mapping, reviewed normalized offers, duplicate/update decisions and immutable accepted revisions.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Excel parser and storage selection assigned to architecture/import specification.

capability_assessments.need: Conditional form editor and runtime mechanisms
capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Forms mechanisms may render, validate and edit schemas; Calculator Design owns branches, selected item references, quantities, band rules and publication semantics.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Orbyss Forms candidate; renderer/backend and exact package closure require architecture selection.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Catalog owns Dutch/English/French/German item meaning, write/import validation and immutable label revisions; adapter uses reusable catalog mechanisms.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Orbyss Localization candidate; durable storage and version compatibility assigned to architecture.

capability_assessments.need: Translated calculator text authoring and runtime
capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Own form/brand/classification language content; writes and publication pin immutable revisions. Estimation preserves resolved historical text through the recipe bridge.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Orbyss Localization and Forms bridge candidates; regional/fallback details assigned to feature specification.

capability_assessments.need: Branding, accessible browser layouts and distribution
capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Organization owns brand and published identities; UI profile supplies tokens/accessibility guidance. Public journey and admin shell share meaning across hosted/embedded delivery.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: ui-experience-v1; native CSS tokens and Lucide default; consumer-owned embed adapter.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Managed session and HTTP authorization mechanisms; organization settings own publishing/admin grants, and every context enforces its organization/resource permissions.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: bff-cookie-v1 default; identity provider and deployment claim mappings assigned to architecture.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Own quantity execution, comparable-price eligibility, min/max/mean aggregation, total-range percentage bands and missing-price completeness.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Project-owned deterministic estimator; bounded rule mechanism defined in feature specification.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Own immutable answers, selected items, quantities, historical labels, totals and revision references; admin retrieval cannot silently recalculate.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Durable consumer-owned persistence; architecture selects provider and owner-local atomicity.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Own historical consumer-safe output and access policy; account/email are not prerequisites and supplier details are excluded.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: PDF renderer and download mechanism assigned to architecture/result feature.

capability_assessments.semantic_profile: Downstream-owned queries translate exact recipe and catalog revisions; upstream retains data ownership and Estimation owns submission consistency/failure handling.
capability_assessments.provider_selection: Consumer bridges; no cross-context store access or atomic writes.

boundary_challenges.concern: Supplier is a noun and possible future portal, not automatically a separate bounded context.
boundary_challenges.finding: Keep suppliers and item-code mapping together while the intermediary owns comparability and acceptance; split only on an independent supplier lifecycle.

boundary_challenges.concern: A central admin screen and independently hosted admin app are not a distinct business model.
boundary_challenges.finding: Admin workflows enter the owning Catalog, Calculator Design or Estimation context; organization publishing settings remain a module. Every context owns its resource rules.

boundary_challenges.concern: History, PDF and access controls could become unnecessary separate contexts.
boundary_challenges.finding: Keep snapshots, admin review and consumer export within the same estimate lifecycle. Split only if an independently owned reporting or quotation model emerges.

boundary_challenges.concern: Generic Forms and Localization mechanisms could absorb item, pricing or release semantics.
boundary_challenges.finding: Catalog owns item language; Calculator Design owns form/brand/band text and publication; Estimation owns historical resolved text. Mechanism adapters support explicit writes and reads without new business contexts.

subdomains.name: Item Catalog
subdomains.vision: Define comparable products and services across industries.
subdomains.ownership: Canonical item identity, category hierarchy, typed properties and units.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not own supplier product codes or estimate arithmetic.
invariants: Item meaning is organization-owned and industry-configurable.

subdomains.name: Supplier Data Acquisition
subdomains.vision: Turn supplier spreadsheets into traceable comparable offers.
subdomains.ownership: Supplier entities, code mappings, review and eligible prices.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not select suppliers for consumers.
invariants: Unresolved mappings cannot silently influence estimates.

subdomains.name: Guided Calculator Modeling
subdomains.vision: Express an industry's estimation journey through reusable configuration.
subdomains.ownership: Branches, item selections, quantity rules, classification labels and release meaning.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not own generic form-renderer source.
invariants: Renovation is configuration, not a hard-coded product limit.

subdomains.name: Organization Publishing
subdomains.vision: Publish private organization configuration as branded public calculators.
subdomains.ownership: Branding, calculator identity, language content and publication/distribution settings.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not create a supplier marketplace.
invariants: Public publication exposes only approved consumer-facing data.

subdomains.name: Authentication, Forms and Localization Mechanisms
subdomains.vision: Use reusable authentication, rendering, editing and language delivery machinery.
subdomains.ownership: Technical mechanisms mediated by domain-owned adapters.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not own customer permissions, pricing, item language or publication semantics.
invariants: Mechanism adoption never transfers consumer business ownership.

subdomains.name: Budget Estimation
subdomains.vision: Convert selected items and quantities into useful indicative budget ranges.
subdomains.ownership: Aggregation, completeness, total-range classification and immutable result meaning.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not promise a binding quote or a jointly available supplier bundle.
invariants: Total endpoints sum eligible line endpoints; unknown prices remain explicit.

subdomains.name: Result Review and Export
subdomains.vision: Make an estimate usable after submission without exposing suppliers.
subdomains.ownership: Admin history, consumer projections and PDF rendering from saved results.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not silently recalculate old results.
invariants: Consumer exports contain no supplier identities.

candidate_contexts.name: Catalog
candidate_contexts.vision: Provide a private, comparable, revisioned catalog of items and supplier offers.
responsibilities: Own internal item codes, typed category properties, units and translated item meaning.
Own suppliers, code mappings, Excel review and eligible offer revisions.
invariants: Every mapped offer belongs to the same organization as its internal item.
Only compatible, reviewed offers become eligible; supplier codes are not internal item identity.
candidate_contexts.lifecycle: Draft/imported -> mapped and validated -> accepted revision -> superseded.
candidate_contexts.separation_rationale: Catalog meaning and import eligibility share one administrator but change independently of published recipes and completed results.
split_triggers: Independent supplier onboarding, commercial negotiation or catalog governance becomes a separate business lifecycle.

candidate_contexts.name: Calculator Design
candidate_contexts.vision: Let organization admins publish reusable, branded estimation journeys across industries.
responsibilities: Own conditional form meaning, quantity rules, bands, calculator identity and release policy.
Own customer settings, four-language calculator text, release pinning and distribution configuration.
non_responsibilities: Supplier offer editing or canonical item ownership.
Persisted consumer estimate identity or recalculation history.
invariants: A release references validated same-organization catalog and content revisions.
No public access to admin credentials, draft definitions or private supplier data.
candidate_contexts.lifecycle: Draft -> validate -> preview -> published release -> retired.
candidate_contexts.separation_rationale: Authoring and publication have a separate model and lifecycle from supplier imports and immutable estimate results.
split_triggers: Organization management develops independent billing/provisioning semantics.
Generic translation lifecycle needs an independently owned service.

candidate_contexts.name: Estimation
candidate_contexts.vision: Produce understandable, historically stable budget estimates from published calculator recipes.
responsibilities: Own evaluation, min/max/mean aggregation, completeness and total-range classifications.
Own estimate snapshots, admin history and consumer PDF/read projections.
non_responsibilities: Supplier selection, quotation acceptance, ordering or payments.
invariants: Every result uses one coherent published recipe and exact catalog revision.
Missing prices never silently mean zero; consumer results omit supplier identities.
A stored estimate is not rewritten by later content or price publication.
candidate_contexts.lifecycle: Published form opened -> answers submitted -> evaluated -> snapshot saved -> viewed/exported.
candidate_contexts.separation_rationale: Execution and historical result identity differ from both authoring state and mutable upstream offers.
split_triggers: Independent quotation, procurement or lead lifecycle is explicitly added.
History becomes a separately owned reporting product.

founding_decision_candidates.title: Separate Catalog, Calculator Design and Estimation
founding_decision_candidates.question: Where do item meaning, published calculator configuration and historical results belong?
founding_decision_candidates.recommended_option: Use three explicit domain boundaries in an initially modular application, with modules inside each context.
alternatives: Keep all behavior in one cohesive context until independent ownership emerges.
Deploy separate business services for catalog, authoring and estimates.
founding_decision_candidates.rationale: Imported mutable supply data, published recipes and immutable estimate results have different language and lifecycle; hosting differences alone do not create business contexts.
consequences: Requires three versioned consumer-owned read bridges.
Avoid independent service operations until workload or ownership proves the need.
Split supplier management only when its lifecycle becomes independent.

founding_decision_candidates.title: Pin published revisions and preserve estimate meaning
founding_decision_candidates.question: How can imports, translations, publication and estimate history remain coherent without cross-context atomic writes?
founding_decision_candidates.recommended_option: Catalog creates immutable reviewed revisions; Calculator Design atomically activates a recipe that pins catalog/content revisions; Estimation reads those exact revisions and locally saves the result.
alternatives: Resolve latest accepted catalog revision once at submission and pin it only in the result.
Copy catalog data into each calculator release through a coordinated publication process.
founding_decision_candidates.rationale: Explicit publication and immutable saved results need stable interpretation even when prices or translations later change.
consequences: Accepted price changes require a new calculator activation before public use under this proposal.
Cross-context dependencies are read-only; only the owning context writes its data.
Missing revisions fail visibly; retention must preserve references until dependent results can stand alone.

founding_decision_candidates.title: Share calculator behavior across hosted and embedded delivery
founding_decision_candidates.question: How should one calculator support a full web app, embedding and independent admin hosting?
founding_decision_candidates.recommended_option: Keep public calculator execution and domain contracts shared; separate admin/public web composition, with one hosted app delivered first and an isolated embed adapter delivered next within launch scope.
alternatives: Build separate standalone and embedded calculator implementations.
Distribute a host-page widget that shares the customer's page styling and runtime.
founding_decision_candidates.rationale: E6 requires both modes at launch in sequence and allows separate admin hosting; shared execution avoids divergence in quantities, prices and localized results.
consequences: Embedding transport, origins, resizing/accessibility and browser behavior require an architecture compatibility spike.
Public use cannot require the admin session; admin retains the managed BFF profile.

founding_decision_candidates.title: Use managed mechanisms without transferring business ownership
founding_decision_candidates.question: Which responsibilities belong to reusable Forms/Localization mechanisms versus this product?
founding_decision_candidates.recommended_option: Adapt Orbyss Forms and Localization through owned Catalog/Calculator Design modules; keep item, quantity, price, language meaning, publication and snapshot rules in consumer contexts.
alternatives: Implement custom form editing/rendering and localization mechanisms.
Adopt a third-party hosted form service and translate its contracts into the same domain model.
founding_decision_candidates.rationale: The installed capability catalog declares these mechanisms, while the product's generic industry semantics and price ownership remain explicit.
consequences: Architecture must verify renderer/backend/storage and package compatibility before selection.
Authentication uses the applicable managed BFF default for admin, independent of anonymous embedding.
If .NET is selected, the managed external Foundation.Host default applies; no user stack preference is invented.

founding_decision_candidates.title: Preserve organization and consumer visibility boundaries
founding_decision_candidates.question: How should central administration coexist with public no-account estimates?
founding_decision_candidates.recommended_option: All authoring and supplier records remain scoped to an organization; Estimation exposes a separate consumer-safe projection while admins access authorized saved snapshots.
alternatives: Dedicated application/database deployments for every organization.
Shared public supplier/catalog records with customer-specific filters.
founding_decision_candidates.rationale: Users explicitly selected private organization data, public basic estimation and no supplier-consumer interaction.
consequences: Organization/resource authorization applies in every context, import and historical lookup.
Download access without an account needs an explicit bounded access design.
Physical data isolation and provisioning are architecture/deployment choices, not inferred shared-data permission.

open_items.question: Which backend/frontend, identity, durable storage and managed renderer/package combination realizes the proposed model?
open_items.disposition: Architecture phase compares compatible options and records Proposed ADRs plus package/provider selection; no user technology preference is assumed.

open_items.question: Which embed mechanism supports customer sites and independently hosted admin with shared execution?
open_items.disposition: Architecture phase compares isolated frame-style embedding with a host-page widget and verifies browser/accessibility/origin behavior.
open_items.trigger: Architecture phase; delivery follows hosted proving journey but remains launch scope.

open_items.question: What exact template, typed attribute constraints, validity, unit/tax normalization, duplicate/update and mapping diagnostics are required?
open_items.disposition: Catalog/import feature specification defines examples and invariants with the product owner; no incompatible row silently becomes eligible.
open_items.trigger: First Catalog and supplier import feature specifications.

open_items.question: What rule vocabulary, branching/backtracking, rounding, repeated selections and zero-width range behavior implement the accepted calculations?
open_items.disposition: Calculator/Estimation specifications define bounded rules and examples without industry-specific hard coding or changing accepted arithmetic.

open_items.question: How are pinned releases, in-flight sessions, idempotent submissions and owner-local failure/retry semantics realized?
open_items.disposition: Architecture must challenge revision-pinning candidate and record consistency ADR; publication/estimation specs implement the exact protocol.

open_items.question: Which regional formatting, fallback and translation editing/import validation rules apply to the four named languages?
open_items.disposition: Localization/content specifications define these with organization content owners; all four named languages remain launch requirements.
open_items.trigger: First localization/content specification; approved content before customer onboarding.

open_items.question: What bounded download access and admin-history permissions preserve private data without consumer accounts?
open_items.disposition: Estimation/result specification defines download access, expiration and projection tests; no unrestricted public historical listing is inferred.

open_items.question: What hosting location, workload limits, retention/deletion and backup/recovery policies apply?
open_items.disposition: Business owner and delivery team set production policy before onboarding or storing production data; use synthetic data for initial proving work.
open_items.blocks: Production readiness, not intake or synthetic proving slice.
open_items.trigger: Before production deployment and data onboarding.

open_items.question: How are organizations/admins provisioned and brand assets, translations and embed origins supplied?
open_items.disposition: Delivery team and business owner define the onboarding workflow in the first administration specification; identity provider selected by architecture.
open_items.trigger: Administration feature specification and before production onboarding.

open_items.question: When should suppliers upload their own Excel sheets?
open_items.disposition: Product owner commissions a later release after administrator imports/template are proven; intermediary review precedes price activation.
open_items.trigger: After the admin import workflow is proven and the release is explicitly commissioned.

open_items.question: When are custom calculator domains or more band presentation modes needed?
open_items.disposition: Product owner can commission custom domains, item-level bands or absolute boundaries later; hosted links and embedding remain included now.
open_items.trigger: Explicit customer requirement beyond accepted initial delivery.

journeys.statement: Organization admin defines items for its industry. Outcome: Private categorized items, units, typed properties and four-language labels are saved or visibly rejected.

Supplier provides a sheet and the organization admin imports it. Outcome: Mapped comparable supplier offers form an accepted catalog revision, or the admin sees validation issues without corrupting the prior revision.

Organization admin prepares a named branded calculator. Outcome: A validated four-language calculator release is available through its hosted link, with coherent item, price and content revision references.
Intermediary walks through a renovation with the consumer. Outcome: Consumer receives a saved indicative renovation estimate and sees whether the selected work fits the budget.

Consumer opens a branded hosted calculator without an account. Outcome: Consumer independently receives a saved localized itemized estimate with min/max, optional mean, bands and any incomplete-price indication.

Website publisher embeds a calculator; a consumer uses it on the existing website. Outcome: Consumer completes the same branded estimation journey inside the customer website; admin hosting can remain separate.

Authenticated organization admin selects a saved estimate. Outcome: Admin sees the original answers, items, quantities, language and prices within its own organization despite later catalog or form changes.
Consumer chooses PDF download after a submission. Outcome: Consumer receives a PDF of the saved estimate without an account/email requirement or supplier identities.
